why: The criterion holds for all six expect lines. Four are CLI runs at the PR head (`--shout Ann`, `Ann --shout`, plain `Ann`, `--shout` with no name). Each has a "run" proof that gives exact output and an exit code, using od -c with PIPESTATUS, or a command substitution followed by $?. Each run has one clear answer. The docs line checks docs/index.md in the repo with a "read" proof ("Read docs/index.md at the PR head"), not the live site. The test line uses `npm test` plus grep and a read of test/greet.test.js, all available before merge. Checking the published site is moved into non_goals ("happens after merge"), so no expect line depends on a deploy, a release or a published page. The upper-case checks are specific enough that one careful reader would reach one answer.
